speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you tell me if you have experienced any recent head injuries, neck stiffness, or a severe headache? Also, have you noticed any sensitivity to light or sounds?

text: 22-year-old male. The patient presents with a 2-day history of fever and altered mentation, reporting fever without chills and rigors. He denies sore throat, abdominal pain, headache, loose stool, burning micturition, or seizures. Has a history of tics and is currently taking haloperidol.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of tics and current use of haloperidol, I need to rule out a drug-induced movement disorder. Have you experienced any muscle rigidity, tremors, or involuntary movements, and have you noticed any changes in your sweating or heart rate?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever and altered mentation. I also have Profuse sweating, Generalized rigidity, Confusion and disorientation, Ability to move all limbs, Normal deep tendon reflexes with bilateral downgoing plantar responses.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the fever, altered mentation, generalized rigidity, and profuse sweating in the context of haloperidol use, I need to check for autonomic instability and muscle damage. REQUEST TEST: Creatine Kinase, Complete Blood Count, Electrolytes, Metabolic Panel

text: RESULTS: Creatine Kinase: 5600 U/L (elevated); Complete Blood Count: White Blood Cell Count 14,700/mm3 (elevated); Electrolytes: Data not provided; Metabolic Panel: Data not provided

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a history of recent changes in your haloperidol dosage, or have you started any new medications recently? I also need to know if you have experienced any difficulty swallowing or changes in your blood pressure and heart rate.

text: The elevated creatine kinase and leukocytosis, combined with fever, rigidity, and altered mentation in a patient on haloperidol, strongly suggest Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome.
